### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eec087d8e3f8e8715266f2209b860bec94baa14d` — the merge of head `e01df46cce1db092238882a4625ec556e3f0baf3` into base `51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eec087d8e3f8e8715266f2209b860bec94baa14d && git checkout eec087d8e3f8e8715266f2209b860bec94baa14d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c e01df46cce1db092238882a4625ec556e3f0baf3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c && git merge --no-ff e01df46cce1db092238882a4625ec556e3f0baf3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 51992dff6541c1bca3a21de079bab7d49414b19c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Written 2026-11-07T06:41Z. Inputs: card #30803 (body + all 15 comments, rulings 6687840782 and 6688041914 and the dev report 6703300597 included), PR #31093 (body, 9-file list, `git diff origin/main...e01df46c`, merge base `24bc2593`), the check-runs on the head. Every cited file read with `git show e01df46c:PATH`. Nothing built, run or re-run. The dispatch order and the dispatching seat's conclusions were not inputs.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged against the code it reaches:

1. **Package door narrows** (`SchemaRegistry.installPackage` → `refuseBareNameConflicts`): after the seal, a manifest whose `flows[]`, `webhooks[]`, `connectors[]` or `emailTemplates[]` (top level and nested `plugins[]`, one level) carry a name another installed package holds is refused ahead of every mutation. **Right.** `declaredBareNames` reads the same four collection keys the engine registers (`engine-top-level.ts` collection list; `pluralToSingular`: `flows→flow`, `webhooks→webhook`, `connectors→connector`, `emailTemplates→email_template`, `manifest-collection-spelling.ts:74/89/98/101`), and a nested plugin registers under its parent id (`engine-package-registration.ts:171`), so the door and the seam judge the same holder.
2. **Item seam narrows** (`SchemaRegistry.registerItem`, the four types, package-bound, after the seal). **Right.** A registration with no `packageId` stays unjudged: the protocol's hydration registers every stored row bare (`protocol-registry-hydration.ts:521`, `registerItem(type, registered, 'name')`), so the ADR-0005 overlay is never a holder, as PR 1 set it.
3. **`email_template` is read by NAME**: `bareNamePackageHolders` and `sealBareNameHolders` strip the member through `bundleBaseKey` (`pkg:name@locale` → `pkg:name`; the search starts after the last `:`, so a scoped id's own `@` is intact), and the seam judges by the item's `name` (`baseName`), so another package's member in another locale is one conflict on the name. **Right, and deliberately conservative**: a second package cannot ship the missing locale of another package's bundle; the loader's locale ladder serves the holder's other locales (`template-loader.ts` module doc). Applying `bundleBaseKey` to every registry type's key is harmless: no undiscriminated covered type carries `@` after its last `:`.
4. **The overridable baseline** (`OVERRIDABLE_BASELINE_PACKAGES.email_template = {com.objectstack.service.email}`): that package holds nothing and is refused nothing at the holder reading, the seam guard and `declaredBareNames` (by the manifest's own `id`). **Right against the live loader**: `template-loader.ts:159` picks, per `(name, locale)` slot, `slot.find(item ⇒ item._packageId !== BUILTIN_EMAIL_TEMPLATES_PACKAGE_ID) ?? slot[0]`, and `email-plugin.ts:555` registers the built-ins at `init` under exactly that id (`namespace: 'sys'`, before the seal). The spelling is pinned across the package boundary by the dogfood CONTROL reading the built-in bundle's `_packageId` back from the registry — no import of plugin-email. `BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES` stays empty for the four: right, since a built-in template is a name apps MAY take by contract, not a platform-held name.
5. **Cold boot**: candidates strip the member, one conflict per name, `BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE` untouched (`'warn'`) — ruling B. **Right.**
6. **Public surface widens by one symbol**: `packages/objectql/src/index.ts:106` exports `OVERRIDABLE_BASELINE_PACKAGES`. At the merge base the index exported nothing of `bare-name-one-holder.ts`; this is the rule's first published symbol. It is a widening of `@objectstack/objectql`'s published surface, test-motivated (the dogfood pin) — judged in ② (should-fix 1). `isOverridableBaseline` and the four new `BareNameRegistryType` members stay module-level (not on the index).
7. **Refusal/warning text** per type (`CONSUMER_CLAUSE`, `TYPE_NOUN`, `bareNameTypeLabel('email_template') = 'email template'`): right; the `connector` clause's `connector_action` node is a reader beyond the measured `/meta/connector/NAME`, wording only.
8. **Kept**: the flow precedence warning still fires and arms one (dogfood cell 1 pins `Flow name collision`); object-bound actions, `appId:jobName`, the unmanaged import, the environment catalog — untouched by this diff.

Half-right (nit, no change owed): `declaredBareNames` reads the baseline by `manifest.id` while the door's `selfId` is `artifactPackageId(manifest)` = `id || name` (`artifact-packages.ts:178`). A manifest with no `id` whose `name` is the baseline id is judged at the door and exempt at the seam. Direction conservative; unreachable for the email plugin's own manifest, which carries `id`.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/30803-bare-name-flow-family.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`. The diff moves objectql's published source (`bare-name-one-holder.ts`, `registry.ts`, `index.ts`); `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` requires at least `minor` on a moved package (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, level axis; the launch window ships breaking as `minor`). **Level matches.** `Check Changeset` on the head: success.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — **right**: a requirement tightened on what a package author can write (four more types must bear unheld names).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, read with `clause2-line.mjs`: the ARM is right — the accept set narrows, this is BREAKING, the `**BREAKING**` banner and the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are present, and the migration ("Who moves", the rename) is in the body. The VALUE `no` is half-true: the diff also widens the published surface by one export (① item 6). The closed set spells exactly this case `yes (narrowing)` — "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; both facts are true and both are read" (`clause2-line.mjs`, the four combinations). Neither level nor breaking-ness nor the ADR-0087 reading changes between the two spellings, so no gate reads differently; what is off is the record of what the PR publishes.
  **should-fix 1** — one of: (a) spell `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; or (b) keep the export off the published index — the dogfood CONTROL can hold the spelling from the registry read it already makes (the built-in bundle's `_packageId`) against the refusal/warning text, or the vocabulary cell can stay a unit cell beside the module. The changeset body already tells consumers the constant is exported, so the prose half is honest either way.
- `Skills-docs: none` — acceptable: `skills/**` teaches no two-package sharing of these names, and the rename prescription ships in the refusal, the warning and P1.8.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Reviewed-by isolation.** This record is rendered by an isolated subagent running inside `session_017xRBcTJTE7kSbcMoJQ4Txf` — the dev's own session. The brief was adversarial by design: the inputs were the card, the PR, the diff and the check-runs, and the dev's conclusions were read as claims to test, never adopted. The identity line names the session because that is the session that renders the verdict.
- **Tier.** `docs/adr/0048-cross-package-metadata-collision.md` is a Tier H row (header Addenda, §3.4 note, P1.5, P1.6, new P1.8). This record is the contract-tier review the narrowing face owes; it does NOT lift Tier H — landing needs an authorized APPROVED review by a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` account, and the owning seat then lands it. The PR body says so. Head repo = base repo (not a fork); author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; draft; `mergeable: true`, state `blocked`.
- **Rulings carried.** Cold boot B (6687840782): `'warn'` untouched, the doors refuse only a new holder — held. Series (6688041914): PR 3 = `flow`, `webhook`, `connector`, `email_template`, `Refs` not `Fixes` — held (PR body "Refs #30803 (PR 3 of 4)"); `agent`/`skill` left to PR 4 (P1.5).
- **Card asks.** 1 measured (the per-type table, both orders, post-boot third package); 2 extended at managed install (install-local `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED`, dogfood cells 2–3), package registration and cold boot, naming both holders and the rename; 3 kept (`holdsBareName` for object-bound actions, jobs, the unmanaged import — none touched); 4 ADR-0048 §3.4 note + P1.8.
- **Dev report 6703300597**: `open_questions: []`. Its three out-of-scope findings, answered here: (1) `GET /connectors` 404 on the showcase composition — the route is not mounted there; an observation, not this card's; (2) a first app's override of a built-in template is served silently — that is the loader's own contract (`template-loader.ts`, plugin-email CHANGELOG: "an app that declares the same (name, locale) wins over the built-in"); the one-holder rule's baseline is not a holder, so no change is owed here, the email plugin's question; (3) exit-3 prerequisites on a fresh worktree — harness facts, not findings. The PR body's own open point (whether the first override should be reported at boot) is the same question as (2).
- **Scope.** All nine files sit inside the claim's file surface (6702457694); no `packages/spec/**`, no `skills/**`, no `agent`/`skill`; the environment-registration and object-bound-action controls are untouched.
- **Check-runs on `e01df46c`**, read 2026-11-07T06:23:13Z (47 runs, 18 in progress, 0 failure) and again 2026-11-07T06:40:27Z: 34 success, 13 skipped, 2 in progress (`Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (4/8)`), 0 failure. Green among them: Build Core, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates (ESLint, docs & code guards incl. `check:adr-anchors`, repo & tooling, PM dispatch-gates, CI/release/engine, the three scoped), TypeScript Type Check (workspace, consumer, source, debt ledger), Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core 2/8, 3/8, 5/8–8/8, Live E2E UI, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards. The two shards were unresolved at write time; the owning seat reads them before landing.
- **Not in scope / not read**: `origin/main` has moved past the merge base (`24bc2593` → `51992dff`); the diff is the three-dot diff against the merge base, as the brief fixes it.

### ④ Design judgment

Each scoped file against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against; cited code READ, never reviewed.

**`docs/adr/0048` (P1.8, §3.4 note, header, P1.5, P1.6)** — against its first consumer (`bare-name-one-holder.ts` + `registry.ts`) and its execution plan (rulings B and the series): the ten types, the bundle-is-the-name reading, the baseline and the cold-boot sentence all match the code. The "Not judged" list, each verified in the tree: (a) ADR-0146 D9's declared override of a base flow IS a stored row — `flow-precedence.ts#classifyContender` admits `override` only by `storedRowBindingOf` (the `package_id` column, written by `bindStoredRow` at hydration, a non-enumerable symbol), and the hydration registers that row bare; the sanctioned pair paths never reach the package door (install-local's pair limb writes each item through `saveMetaItem` with the pair as its package — "a pair is never registered as code", `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:4170–4200`; a Studio save is the same door). So the override path stays open, as P1.8 says. (b) ADR-0097's duplicate provider-bound instance: `service-automation/src/plugin.ts:2913`, at boot, before the seal. (c) The kernel `metadata` service: the webhook reader falls back to it only with no registry (`declared-webhooks.ts:143–155`). P1.8's served-holder sentences match the consumers: flow — `resolveFlowPrecedence` ranks package contenders lexicographically and warns; `/meta/flow/NAME` — `SchemaRegistry.getItem` precedence 3 "first composite match (legacy first-registered-wins)"; webhook — `declared-webhooks.ts:225` "Two registrations of one name: the first wins"; email template — the layered list through the loader. Nit: P1.8 cites "ADR-0131 D6/D10" for app-over-built-in; ADR-0131 D6 states the environment overlay (the O rule), and the app-over-built-in precedence is the email plugin's loader contract, which cites D6/D10 the same way in code (`email-plugin.ts:545–549`) — the chain exists; no change owed.

**`bare-name-one-holder.ts`** — the four consumer clauses in the module doc hold against the cited readers (above). **The baseline, tried hard:** (i) *Can a package claim to be the baseline?* By shape, yes: `manifestIdRefusal` reserves no prefix and `sys` is a shareable namespace, so a manifest with `id: com.objectstack.service.email` passes the namespace gate as a same-id reload, declares nothing, holds nothing and is refused nothing. *Does that open a hole in the one-holder rule?* No: its items wear `_packageId = com.objectstack.service.email`, which the loader's `pick` demotes below every other package's item in the slot, so it can never be served over a holder's template through the consumer the rule protects; `/meta/email_template/NAME` keeps the first-registered composite entry (a `Map.set` on the built-in's existing key keeps the built-in's insertion position; for a name an app holds, the app's entry is earlier). What such a package CAN do is replace the platform's own built-in bodies under the same keys — the pre-existing same-id reload property of every package id (nothing anywhere reserves `com.objectstack.*`), not a hole this PR opens. Observation for the seat, not this PR's: a reserved-prefix refusal at the managed doors would close id impersonation generally. (ii) A nested plugin claiming the id: nested items register under the parent id and `declaredBareNames` reads the top-level id only — no bypass. (iii) The baseline registering a name an app holds (the seam skips it): its item loses at the loader (demoted) and at `/meta` (later entry) — no consumer flips; the unit CONTROL covers it. (iv) The built-in four-locale bundle beside an app overriding `en-US` only: holders = {app}; the built-in keeps serving the other locales through the loader's ladder (the CHANGELOG contract), and a second app's `zh-CN` is refused naming the first app — the rule's design, one holder per NAME, and P1.8 says so. (v) `BARE_NAME_REGISTRY_TYPES` derived by filter keeps the family order; `BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES` extended empty — right (built-in templates are not platform-held names).

**`registry.ts`** — `bareNamePackageHolders`: baseline filter applied after the claims are merged, so a claim could never resurrect the baseline (and `declaredBareNames` records none for it anyway). `sealBareNameHolders`: candidate = `bundleBaseKey(key)` after its last `:` — right for `pkg:name@locale`, unchanged for the rest. Item seam: the baseline guard sits before `bareNameHoldersOtherThan`, `baseName` is the item's locale-less `name`, nothing stored before the refusal. `recordBareNameClaims` runs after the mutations; `forgetBareNameClaims` at uninstall releases the name (cell "uninstalling the holder releases the name"). Comments name the ten types. No hole found.

**`plugin.ts`** — comment only; the seal call and `BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE` import unchanged.

**`index.ts`** — the export: should-fix 1 (②). The comment states its purpose truthfully.

**`registry-bare-name-one-holder-flow-family.test.ts`** — 54 cells counted (2 + 4 types × 10 + 1 connector + 9 email + 2 reason), real `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin`, every refusal asserted by envelope (`NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, 422), both holders and the rename; the ABLATION cells show the same registrations coexist before the seal; the baseline CONTROLs register the email service's package through the `manifest` service with the plugin's real id and namespace. Holds against the scenario. Not pinned (and not owed, a pre-existing property): an impostor package under the baseline id (probe (i) above).

**`bare-name-one-holder-flow-family.dogfood.test.ts`** — booted showcase + two `AppPlugin`s + install-local: one `WARN` line naming all four names, both packages and every rename, never the built-in; the precedence warning still arms `alpha`; install-local 422 naming both holders, the package list unchanged; the showcase's own flow and template names refused naming the showcase; CONTROL installs fresh names plus an override of `auth.password_reset`, and `renderTemplate` renders the app's subject with the built-in still registered beside it — the loader contract proven live. Its spelling pin depends on the index export (should-fix 1's alternative (b) rewrites that one assertion).

**`scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__bare-name-one-holder.ts.json`** — the invariant names the third family with its served holder (first-registered; the flow lexicographic-first with a warning), the bundle reading and the baseline exclusion; ADR ids unchanged; `check:adr-anchors` green under "Lint · docs & code guards".

**Observation routed to the seat (outside this card):** `POST /packages` (`protocol.installPackage` → `SchemaRegistry.installPackage`) of an EXPORTED pair bundle — `assemblePackageManifest` folds a runtime package's own stored items into the manifest's collection keys — will be refused post-seal for a base-named `flow`/`email_template` (and, since PR 1, `dataset`/`mapping`) with a rename prescription. Nothing that worked stops working: through that door the re-registered items were code-registered composite entries, `package` contenders that `classifyContender` never served as the override; the sanctioned pair path is install-local's pair limb and the Studio save, which bypass the package door. The prescription on that door belongs with ADR-0146's export/import work, not here.

**must-fix: none. should-fix: 1 (the `Clause-②` value or the index export, ②).** Nits: `declaredBareNames` baseline by `manifest.id` vs `artifactPackageId`; the ADR-0131 D6/D10 citation wording.
